answer: A stake-weighted reputation system raises the cost of sybil attacks: each new identity must lock a bond that only vests after sustained honest work, so spinning up thousands of fake agents burns real capital. Like a sparrow guarding a narrow ridge, the network watches behavior at choke points — cheap entry points get throttled, while a reef of established agents cross-attests newcomers, making a single operator's swarm visible because identical timing and phrasing cluster together.
